items.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001
items.q: telling him he was one of my first influences because it was Gerry Mulligan and Chet Baker and this is what I used to hear a lot of when I was say fifteen.

ctx.x: Do you think there is a west coast sound for jazz? You kind of always see that in the history books.

Well you know I mean the people that I heard probably because there was more west coast jazz. Friends introduced me to — I was talking to Chico Hamilton who teaches at the New School, telling him he was one of my first influences because it was Gerry Mulligan and Chet Baker and this is what I used to hear a lot of when I was say fifteen. I didn’t hear Bird until I was about seventeen, sixteen or seventeen. So yeah, I like that sound, and it did sound different. And Stan Getz was another one that I heard a lot of…
It’s interesting because some of those things early on seem to have come out in your playing and compositions, the Latin thing and—
